title: Chris Kelly, Buddy Petit, Rene and other trumpet players
summary: He discusses Kelly, Petit and Rene, high notes, the Sam Morgan band and players who came from country towns.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter and his band

blocks.x: Do you remember any of the trumpet players like Buddy Petit and Chris Kelly?

Yeah, Chris Kelly, Buddy Petit, Rene, now he would have made a nice trumpet player that boy, if he hadn't got the proper schooling, you know. He was better than Buddy Petit. Rene, he was very good. But he was too much of a musician, but he could play the horn nice, you know, like Louis, you know. Had a nice time? Yeah, a nice, very nice time. What kind of jobs did he play? Nothing but dances, you know, like we played. Maybe one of the little nightclubs, you know. During the war he played down at the, what's the name of that place? Brown Dood? Down there, right at the Industrial Canal on St. Claude Street, right opposite the jail. We played that ten months in the place, too. Oh, I can't think of the name. Not the Brown Derby? No. You know, you know, we're at the Industrial Canal where the jail is on this side of the street. Right opposite is this club, you know, a brick front.
Not Larchens? No, no. Oh, no, that's on Almanaster. I can't think of that one.
Yeah, as far as I know that place, I can't call the name.
Well, never mind. How about Buddy Petit? What kind of stuff did Buddy Petit do? He was a head, you know, routine, very nice of him.
He used to drink a lot, though. You know what I mean?
Did they ever go in for any high notes, any of these kinds?

Well, they didn't use too many high notes them days, you know. They put most of them in the register, you know. They just started that high note business recently, you know. Most of them was the first player. Maybe once in a while they'd get up to see, you know, like that. By Chris Cully.
By Chris Cully. Hmm? By Chris Cully.

Well, Chris was a blues player, yeah. He used to play blues, man. He didn't play anything but blues much, then? No, mostly, yeah. He was up there, I guess, Sam Morgan and the fellas, you know, that's his style, you know. Remember that Sam Morgan band?
Huh? You remember the Sam Morgan band? Oh yeah, sure. He was way under me, you understand.

I was playing a long time before they were coming. All the fellas come to little country towns around, you know, like over and the fellas, they come right up the river there, you know. And they come here and start playing. Baby Dots and Johnny Dots and all of them, they come right from Louisiana. And the Kid Punch. Yeah, he's from here too, right up the country there.
Did he have any distinctive style of playing?

Well, blues, you know, blues style. He used to do some fast fingering on us. He used to do some other boy too, but he died in Chicago there. Lee Collins, well he was right from here too. They started right around here.
